quotes.text: Wasted budget, annoyed executives, zero behavior change. The truth, deployment isn't adoption, behavior change is the product.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Core thesis of the episode in one line.

quotes.text: Adoption happens when a specific person does a specific task a new way because it's faster, safer, or clearer.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: You can and you should, but training without use case design is theater. Adults learn to solve their own problems.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: Retrieval is not training. Copilot isn't hoovering your crown jewels into a public model. It's retrieving content your user already has permission to see and using it as context for generation.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

takeaways: Copilot adoption is a behaviour-change project: design role-specific, recurring tasks instead of generic productivity promises.
Leaders who demo their real work live with Copilot, plus a steady comms cadence and champions, create the visible permission that drives MAU.
Fix labels and DLP, embed prompts and Copilot Studio micro-agents in daily workflows, and measure MAU, time to draft and ticket trends.
hook: Many Copilot rollouts light up licenses and then stall with zero behaviour change. This episode is for IT, change and business leaders responsible for Microsoft 365 Copilot adoption. Learn the five failure modes and a practical 90-day plan that turns licenses into measurable everyday habits.
